narrativeBlocks.title: A second child appears
narrativeBlocks.body: Kana'ti and Selu's son tells them that a playmate comes out of the water and calls himself his elder brother.

narrativeBlocks.title: The story explains the brother's origin
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Mooney's English record (whitespace normalized): “Then they knew that the strange boy had sprung from the blood of the game which Selu had washed off at the river's edge.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A second origin follows
narrativeBlocks.body: Later in the same narrative, Selu says corn will grow wherever her body is dragged and tells the boys to save seed for planting.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep this account situated
narrativeBlocks.body: Mooney records this tale in his 1902 collection of Cherokee stories. It is a historical English record with an ethnographic frame, not a statement about every Cherokee community today.

narrativeBlocks.title: One narrative links food and kinship
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale connects the origin of game with the origin and planting of corn; keep those events within this recorded story.
